The apparatus includes two vise mechanisms arranged around the cutting position. A feed vise mechanism is provided upstream of the cutting position, and a downstream vise mechanism is provided just downstream of the cutting position.

The feed vise mechanism includes a first feed vise jaw and a second feed vise jaw. The first feed vise jaw is movable by a feed-side moving cylinder so as to clamp and release a workpiece. The second feed vise jaw is shiftable by a feed-side shifting cylinder, allowing the feed vise mechanism to adjust its gripping position relative to the workpiece and the cutting position.

The downstream vise mechanism is arranged on the downstream side of the cutting position and includes a first downstream vise jaw and a second downstream vise jaw. The first downstream vise jaw is movable by a downstream moving cylinder so as to clamp and release the workpiece on the downstream side of the cut. The second downstream vise jaw is shiftable by a downstream shifting cylinder, thereby enabling positional adjustment of the downstream vise mechanism.

The vise surface of the second downstream vise jaw is arranged such that, when the downstream shifting cylinder reaches its stroke end on one side, the vise surface is positioned on one side of a vise reference position. This positioning allows the downstream vise jaw to assume a defined location relative to the reference position when the shifting cylinder is fully actuated in that direction.

In addition, the thrust force generated by the downstream shifting cylinder toward the one side is set to be equal to the thrust force generated by the downstream moving cylinder toward the opposite side. By making these thrust forces equal, the apparatus can balance the forces acting on the downstream vise jaws during clamping and shifting operations, thereby helping to maintain stable positioning and reliable holding of the workpiece near the cutting position.
outputs.L4:
A feed/clamp apparatus for cutting operations is designed to accurately position, hold, and advance a workpiece or bar material as it is cut at a predetermined cutting position. The apparatus includes an upstream feed vise mechanism located on the material-supply side of the cutting position and a downstream vise mechanism located on the discharge side. Together, these mechanisms grip the material before, during, and after cutting so that the material remains stable and properly aligned throughout the cutting cycle.

The upstream feed vise is provided with a pair of feed vise jaws that can open and close around the material. These jaws are moved by a feed vise moving cylinder, allowing the material to be clamped securely when it is being advanced and released when repositioning is required. A feed vise shifting cylinder moves the upstream feed vise mechanism in the feeding direction, thereby advancing the material by a controlled amount toward the cutting position. By repeatedly clamping, shifting, and releasing, the upstream feed vise can feed the material in precise increments for successive cutting operations.

The downstream vise mechanism is positioned on the opposite side of the cutting position and includes first and second downstream vise jaws. These jaws clamp the portion of the material near or beyond the cutting position so that the material is firmly supported during cutting. The first downstream vise jaw is actuated by a moving cylinder, while the second downstream vise jaw is arranged so that it can be positioned with respect to a predetermined reference position. This reference positioning helps ensure that the material is consistently held in the correct location relative to the cutting blade or cutting tool.

A key feature of the apparatus is the manner in which opposing thrust forces in the downstream vise mechanism are balanced. When the downstream vise jaws clamp the material, the actuating cylinders generate thrust forces that can otherwise cause deflection, misalignment, or unstable gripping. In this apparatus, the downstream vise mechanism is constructed so that the thrust force applied to one downstream vise jaw is opposed and balanced by a corresponding thrust force acting in the opposite direction. This balanced force arrangement reduces unwanted displacement of the vise components and helps maintain the material in a stable clamped condition.

By locating the second downstream vise jaw relative to a defined reference position while balancing the thrust forces in the downstream vise mechanism, the apparatus improves cutting accuracy and repeatability. The material is less likely to shift, tilt, or vibrate during cutting, which is especially important when cutting long stock, heavy workpieces, or materials requiring high dimensional precision. As a result, the cut pieces can be produced with improved length accuracy, cleaner cut surfaces, and reduced variation between successive cuts.

In operation, the upstream feed vise grips the material and advances it toward the cutting position by a predetermined feed length. The downstream vise then clamps the material near the cutting position, with its jaws accurately positioned and its internal thrust forces balanced. Once the material is securely held, the cutting operation is performed. After cutting, the vises release and reset as necessary, and the upstream feed vise again advances the remaining material for the next cut.

This feed/clamp apparatus therefore provides a coordinated system for feeding, positioning, and clamping material in cutting equipment such as sawing machines or other industrial cutting machines. Its combination of upstream feeding control, downstream clamping support, reference-based jaw positioning, and balanced thrust force operation contributes to stable material handling and high-precision cutting performance.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common and important words in the English language. Although it is short and simple, it plays a major role in giving meaning and clarity to sentences. The word “the” is called a definite article, which means it is used to refer to a specific person, place, thing, or idea.

For example, when someone says “the book,” they are not talking about just any book. They mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand. This small word helps make communication more precise.

“The” appears in many everyday phrases, such as “the world,” “the future,” “the truth,” and “the best.” It can make a sentence feel complete and focused. Without it, English would often sound unclear or unnatural.

Even though “the” may seem ordinary, it is essential. It connects ideas, identifies specific things, and helps people understand exactly what is being discussed. In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

The apparatus thereby enables accurate feeding, stable clamping, and improved cutting precision.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical description in the style of a Japanese patent translation for a feed vise and downstream vise device, including details about first/second jaws, downstream moving cylinders, downstream shifting cylinders, stroke ends, one-side/another-side movement, and equal thrust force settings.
counterfactuals.output:
A feed vise and downstream vise device is provided for gripping and feeding an elongated workpiece in a longitudinal feed direction, the device comprising a feed vise disposed on an upstream side and a downstream vise disposed on a downstream side in the feed direction.

The feed vise includes a first jaw and a second jaw arranged so as to face each other across a workpiece passage. The first jaw is provided on one side of the workpiece passage, and the second jaw is provided on another side of the workpiece passage. At least one of the first jaw and the second jaw is movable toward and away from the other jaw, whereby the workpiece is selectively clamped and released. The first jaw and the second jaw are configured to grip the workpiece with a predetermined feed gripping force during a feed operation.

The downstream vise includes a downstream first jaw and a downstream second jaw arranged opposite to each other across the workpiece passage on the downstream side of the feed vise. The downstream first jaw is disposed on the one side of the workpiece passage, and the downstream second jaw is disposed on the another side of the workpiece passage. The downstream first jaw and the downstream second jaw are respectively supported so as to be movable in a clamping direction and in a releasing direction.

The downstream vise is provided with downstream moving cylinders for moving the downstream first jaw and the downstream second jaw toward and away from the workpiece. A first downstream moving cylinder is connected to the downstream first jaw, and a second downstream moving cylinder is connected to the downstream second jaw. The first downstream moving cylinder moves the downstream first jaw from a release position to a clamp position on the one side, and the second downstream moving cylinder moves the downstream second jaw from a release position to a clamp position on the another side. The downstream moving cylinders thereby cause the downstream first jaw and the downstream second jaw to clamp the workpiece from both lateral sides.

The downstream vise is further provided with downstream shifting cylinders for shifting the downstream vise, or the downstream first and second jaws, in a lateral direction intersecting the feed direction. The downstream shifting cylinders include a one-side downstream shifting cylinder for applying thrust force in a direction from the another side toward the one side, and an another-side downstream shifting cylinder for applying thrust force in a direction from the one side toward the another side. By operation of the downstream shifting cylinders, the downstream first jaw and the downstream second jaw are shifted together, or the clamped workpiece is shifted together with the downstream vise, toward either the one side or the another side.

Each of the downstream shifting cylinders has a corresponding stroke end. The one-side downstream shifting cylinder has a one-side stroke end defining a terminal position of movement toward the one side, and the another-side downstream shifting cylinder has an another-side stroke end defining a terminal position of movement toward the another side. When the downstream vise is shifted toward the one side, movement is continued until the corresponding cylinder reaches the one-side stroke end. When the downstream vise is shifted toward the another side, movement is continued until the corresponding cylinder reaches the another-side stroke end. Thus, the shifted position of the downstream vise is mechanically determined by the stroke ends of the downstream shifting cylinders.

The downstream moving cylinders and the downstream shifting cylinders are set so that thrust forces exerted in mutually opposed directions are substantially equal. In particular, a thrust force of the one-side downstream shifting cylinder for moving the downstream vise toward the one side and a thrust force of the another-side downstream shifting cylinder for moving the downstream vise toward the another side are set to be equal to each other. Further, thrust forces of the first downstream moving cylinder and the second downstream moving cylinder for closing the downstream first jaw and the downstream second jaw may be set to be equal to each other. Accordingly, when the workpiece is clamped by the downstream vise, displacement of the workpiece toward only one side is suppressed, and the workpiece can be held in a balanced state.

In one embodiment, the downstream first jaw and the downstream second jaw are both movable relative to a downstream vise base. The downstream moving cylinders advance the respective jaws inwardly from opposite sides, while the downstream shifting cylinders shift the downstream vise base or a jaw-supporting member relative to a machine frame. The downstream shifting cylinders are arranged so that one cylinder acts in opposition to the other cylinder, and both cylinders are supplied with pressure adjusted to provide equal thrust force. When the downstream vise is not required to be shifted, the opposed equal thrust forces hold the downstream vise at a neutral position or maintain the downstream vise in a state in which side biasing force is reduced.

In another embodiment, movement toward the one side is performed by extending the one-side downstream shifting cylinder while retracting or permitting movement of the another-side downstream shifting cylinder. Movement toward the another side is performed by extending the another-side downstream shifting cylinder while retracting or permitting movement of the one-side downstream shifting cylinder. The stroke ends of the respective downstream shifting cylinders restrict excessive lateral displacement, whereby positional repeatability of the downstream vise is improved.

The feed vise and the downstream vise may be operated cooperatively. During feeding of the workpiece, the feed vise clamps the workpiece and moves the workpiece in the feed direction while the downstream vise is released. After completion of feeding, the downstream vise clamps the workpiece by operation of the downstream moving cylinders. Thereafter, the feed vise may release the workpiece. When lateral correction or alignment is required, the downstream shifting cylinders shift the downstream vise toward the one side or the another side until the corresponding stroke end is reached. Since the thrust force settings of the opposed downstream shifting cylinders are equalized, variation in lateral pressing force applied to the workpiece is reduced.

According to the above construction, the workpiece can be gripped by the first and second jaws of the feed vise and by the downstream first and second jaws of the downstream vise, and can be shifted to the one side or the another side by the downstream shifting cylinders. Furthermore, by defining movement limits with the stroke ends and by setting opposed thrust forces to be equal, the downstream vise device can reduce unbalanced loading, improve clamping stability, and enhance accuracy in feeding and positioning of the workpiece.
